title: What Does It Take to Be the Best 1v1 Hooper in the World?
summary: With a tournament in Shanghai that went down to the wire, Jordan Brand’s The One Finals crowned the new global champions of the court.
body_markdown:
**On August 29, 16 young players** from cities around the world stepped onto a court in Shanghai for the Jordan Brand The One Finals. Each had fought their way through local qualifiers and semifinals, playing head-to-head past hundreds of young hoopers, to earn a spot among the final eight players in the men’s and women’s divisions.


With no teammates, no substitutions and no collective identity to fall back on, the hoopers waged 1v1 battles to earn a singular title: The One. Watching courtside? The likes of Jayson Tatum, Paolo Banchero, Stephon Castle, Jared McCain, Guo Ailun, Li Tianrong, G.E.M., Jackson Wang, Asen and other members of the Jordan Family, hollering for this next generation as they signaled their futures on the court, letting their game do the talking.


Here, an inside look at what it took to become the champion.
